item.description:
000
ACPN50 PHFO 231726
TWOCP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 AM HST Sun Aug 23 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Lala, located well north of the Papahanaumokuakea Marine
National Monument, on Tropical Storm Moke, located a few hundred
miles south of Hilo, Hawaii, and on newly formed Tropical Storm
Iselle, located several hundred miles south-southwest of the
southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

&&

Public Advisories on Tropical Storm Iselle are issued under WMO
header WTPZ34 NHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP4.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Storm Iselle are issued under WMO
header WTPZ24 and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP4.

$$
Forecaster Hagen

WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 AM HST (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Lala was 
located near latitude 32.5 North, longitude 174.3 West. Lala is 
moving toward the northwest near 5 mph (7 km/h) and this general 
motion is expected to continue for the next several days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 65 mph (100 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Gradual weakening is forecast during the next several days.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 175 miles (280 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 988 mb (29.18 inches).

item.title: Tropical Storm Lala Forecast Discussion Number 46
item.description:
Issued at 1100 AM HST Sun Aug 23 2026 
000
WTPA42 PHFO 232033
TCDCP2
 
Tropical Storm Lala Discussion Number  46
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM HST Sun Aug 23 2026

Visible and infrared satellite imagery shows Tropical Storm Lala may 
be a bit better organized, with deep convection over the center and 
a larger outer band now wrapping around the eastern and northern 
semicircles. The change in appearance has not yet influenced the 
objective and subjective satellite-based intensity estimates, which 
support maintaining an initial intensity of 55 kt for this 
advisory. I again note that this intensity could be generous, but 
is consistent with a steady decay of the cyclone over cooler waters 
and the recent improved appearance on satellite imagery.

Lala's current forward motion is analyzed to be 305/4 kt. The 
mid-level ridge positioned just south and east of the central 
Aleutian Islands is expected to remain the primary steering feature 
through this week. As a result, the tropical storm is forecast to 
continue slowly on a northwestward heading until degenerating into a 
remnant low by 120 h. The track forecast is similar to the previous 
advisory and closely follows the corrected multi-model consensus 
(HCCA), which lies on the western side of the guidance envelope.
 
The intensity forecast is largely unchanged, lies within the middle 
of the guidance envelope near HCCA, and continues to show a slow and 
steady decay as the tropical cyclone moves across gradually cooler 
waters. Some increase in vertical wind shear beginning around 72 h 
should allow mid-level dry air to better penetrate the cyclone. Lala 
is forecast to become a remnant low by 120 h, in agreement with the 
latest GFS and ECMWF simulated satellite imagery, though this could 
happen sooner.

item.description:
Issued at 1100 AM HST Sun Aug 23 2026 
000
WTPA33 PHFO 232032
TCPCP3
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Moke Advisory Number  14
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP022026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM HST Sun Aug 23 2026
 
...HEAVY RAINFALL AND GUSTY WINDS LIKELY OVER THE BIG ISLAND OF
HAWAII TODAY AND TOMORROW...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 AM HST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...15.2N 156.3W
ABOUT 320 MI...515 KM SSW OF HILO HAWAII
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...40 MPH...65 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 275 DEGREES AT 15 MPH...24 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1003 MB...29.62 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 AM HST (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Moke was
located near latitude 15.2 North, longitude 156.3 West. Moke is
moving toward the west near 15 mph (24 km/h), and this general
motion is expected to continue during the next several days. On the
forecast track, the center of the storm is expected to pass south of
the Big Island of Hawaii today, then well south of the smaller
main Hawaiian Islands early next week.

Maximum sustained winds are near 40 mph (65 km/h) with higher gusts.
Moke is forecast to slowly lose strength and could become a 
post-tropical cyclone on Tuesday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 45 miles (75 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1003 mb (29.62 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Tropical Storm Moke can be found in the Tropical
Cyclone Discussion under AWIPS header HFOTCDCP3 and WMO header
WTPA43 PHFO.
 
WIND: Gusty winds are likely across the Hawaiian Islands during
the next couple of days, especially in areas of high terrain.
 
RAINFALL: The tropical storm is expected to produce rainfall totals
of 5 to 10 inches with maximum amounts of 15 inches across the Big
Island. Rainfall totals of 3 to 6 inches are expected on eastern
Maui. These rainfall amounts may produce life-threatening flooding
and mudslides for the windward and southeast Big Island, especially
in steep terrain and over areas that were affected recently by
Lala.
 
Across western Maui and the remainder of the islands, moisture drawn
northward from Moke may bring up to 1 or 2 inches of rain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Moke,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_cp3.shtml?rainqpf.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 500 PM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Blake

item.title: Tropical Storm Moke Forecast Discussion Number 14
item.description:
Issued at 1100 AM HST Sun Aug 23 2026 
000
WTPA43 PHFO 232032
TCDCP3
 
Tropical Storm Moke Discussion Number  14
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP022026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM HST Sun Aug 23 2026
 
A large area of thunderstorm activity continues in the northern
semicircle of Moke, though the southern side of the system remains
mostly exposed. Visible satellite imagery indicates the center is on
the southwestern edge of the deep convection, reflective of the
southerly shear.  While Dvorak intensity estimates have recently
increased, recent scatterometer data is actually lower than 
earlier, showing only a small area of winds above 30 kt.  The 
initial intensity is set to 35 kt assuming some undersampling 
knowing the bias of that instrument. 
 
Moke should move through a tough environment during the next several
days, with lots of mid-level dry air and moderate shear in its path.
These conditions should suppress the influences of the warm
sea-surface temperatures, and Moke will likely only produce
temporary bursts of deep convection early this week.  Shear is 
still forecast to increase in a day or two, and the storm is 
expected to weaken into a tropical depression and/or remnant low 
around that time.  The model trend of an earlier dissipation 
continues, so the time of tropical depression and remnant low 
status has been moved up 12-24 h, with a faster weakening than the 
last advisory.
 
Moke is moving westward at about 13 kt. A strong low- to mid-level
ridge should steer the storm westward to west-northwestward for the
next several days, keeping Moke well south of the main Hawaiian
Islands.  Similar to the last forecast, the model guidance has
shifted a bit to the south, and the NHC track is moved in that
direction. Moke is still expected to pass close enough to the 
Hawaiian Islands to produce a period of gusty winds and heavy 
rainfall across portions of the islands during the next day or two.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Heavy rainfall associated with Tropical Storm Moke is gradually
increasing over the Big Island of Hawaii today. Rain will then
spread westward across the remainder of the Hawaiian Islands through
Monday. This rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and
mudslides for the windward and southeast Big Island, especially in
steep terrain and over areas that were affected recently by Lala.
 
2. Although the strongest winds associated with Moke are expected to
pass south of the Hawaiian Islands, strong gusty winds are likely,
particularly in areas within and downslope of higher terrain.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
